newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT TO DISCUSS NEW PROFIT TAX RULES.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT TO DISCUSS NEW PROFIT TAX RULES.

text.p: The cabinet of ministers is expected to discuss on Wednesday a proposal from the finance ministry to exempt companies from profit tax for three years untill they have covered their losses.
"The amendment would allow the company to transfer its losses to the next year and not to pay profit tax until the losses are covered," the finance ministry said in a statement.
It proposes that losses from one year can be transferred into the following year for a period of three years.
The finance ministry also proposes profit tax be cut to 10 percent from 15 percent for foreign companies if they give Lithuanian firms the right to use their trademarks and licences.
The ministry also proposes a 29 profit tax on payments to foreign companies registered in countries and regions where there is no tax or low tax rates.
